title: Great Books of the Western World
blurb: Britannica's mid-century collection — the long conversation of the West, from Homer to the moderns, gathered as one continuous argument.
about:
Conceived at the University of Chicago by Robert Hutchins and Mortimer Adler and published by Encyclopædia Britannica in 1952, the Great Books of the Western World gathered the central works of Western thought — 54 volumes, Homer to Freud — into a single 'Great Conversation.'

Its spine was the Syntopicon: Adler's vast index of 102 'Great Ideas' that let a reader trace one theme — justice, the soul, time — across three thousand years of authors answering one another. It was the mid-century heir to Eliot's shelf — more philosophical, more systematic — and the foundation of the Great Books movement.

A second edition in 1990 grew the set to sixty volumes, carrying the conversation into the twentieth century. Lectio shelves it in its own volume order — author and principal work, the Greeks to the moderns, each a voice the next one answers.

planned.title: The Greek Tragedies
planned.author: Aeschylus, Sophocles & Euripides
planned.note: The masterpieces of the Athenian stage — Aeschylus, Sophocles, and Euripides on fate, the gods, and the cost of pride.

planned.title: The Histories
planned.author: Herodotus
planned.note: The first work of history — Herodotus on the war between Greece and Persia, and everything he learned along the way.

planned.title: History of the Peloponnesian War
planned.author: Thucydides
planned.note: Thucydides on the war that broke Athens — history written cold, as a possession for all time.

planned.title: Nicomachean Ethics
planned.author: Aristotle
planned.note: Aristotle on virtue and the good life — happiness as the soul's activity in excellence.

planned.title: The Elements
planned.author: Euclid
planned.note: Euclid's geometry — the model of reasoning from first principles that every later science would imitate.

planned.title: The Works of Archimedes
planned.author: Archimedes
planned.note: The greatest mathematician of antiquity — levers, spheres, and the first reach toward the calculus.

planned.title: On the Nature of Things
planned.author: Lucretius
planned.note: Lucretius sets the whole universe in verse — atoms, mortality, and freedom from the fear of death.

planned.title: Lives
planned.author: Plutarch
planned.note: Plutarch's paired lives of Greeks and Romans that taught Europe what greatness looks like.

planned.title: The Annals
planned.author: Tacitus
planned.note: Tacitus on the early Roman emperors — power, fear, and corruption, in the most unsparing prose of antiquity.

planned.title: The Almagest
planned.author: Ptolemy
planned.note: Ptolemy's astronomy — the earth-centered cosmos that ruled the Western mind for fourteen centuries.

planned.title: The Enneads
planned.author: Plotinus
planned.note: Plotinus and the last great vision of pagan philosophy — the soul's ascent toward the One.

planned.title: The City of God
planned.author: Saint Augustine
planned.note: Written as Rome fell — the eternal city of God set against the earthly city of men.

planned.title: Summa Theologica
planned.author: Thomas Aquinas
planned.note: Aquinas's towering synthesis of faith and reason — medieval theology's masterwork.

planned.title: The Divine Comedy
planned.author: Dante Alighieri
planned.note: Dante's journey through Hell, Purgatory, and Paradise — the summit of the medieval imagination.

planned.title: The Canterbury Tales
planned.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
planned.note: Chaucer's pilgrims trade stories on the road to Canterbury — the founding comedy of English literature.

planned.title: On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres
planned.author: Nicolaus Copernicus
planned.note: Copernicus moves the earth — the book that began the scientific revolution.

planned.title: The Prince
planned.author: Niccolò Machiavelli
planned.note: Machiavelli's unflinching handbook of power — how it is really won and kept.

planned.title: Gargantua and Pantagruel
planned.author: François Rabelais
planned.note: Rabelais's giant, riotous satire — learning and appetite, the body and the book, in full Renaissance laughter.

planned.title: The Essays
planned.author: Michel de Montaigne
planned.note: Montaigne invents the essay to study one subject without end — himself — and so discovers all of us.

planned.title: Don Quixote
planned.author: Miguel de Cervantes
planned.note: The first modern novel, entire — a mad knight, his earthbound squire, and the comedy of ideals meeting the world.

planned.title: The Plays and Sonnets
planned.author: William Shakespeare
planned.note: Shakespeare whole — the tragedies, comedies, histories, and sonnets that map the range of what we are.

planned.title: The New Organon
planned.author: Francis Bacon
planned.note: Bacon's manifesto for a new science built on experiment and evidence rather than authority.

planned.title: On the Motion of the Heart and Blood
planned.author: William Harvey
planned.note: Harvey discovers the circulation of the blood — the birth of modern physiology.

planned.title: Two New Sciences
planned.author: Galileo Galilei
planned.note: Galileo founds modern physics — motion and materials, argued in plain dialogue against the schoolmen.

planned.title: Discourse on Method
planned.author: René Descartes
planned.note: Descartes founds modern philosophy on doubt — 'I think, therefore I am.'

planned.title: Leviathan
planned.author: Thomas Hobbes
planned.note: Hobbes on the state of nature and the social contract — life without authority, 'nasty, brutish, and short.'

planned.title: Paradise Lost
planned.author: John Milton
planned.note: Milton's English epic of the fall — Satan, Eden, and the ways of God to men.

planned.title: Pensées
planned.author: Blaise Pascal
planned.note: Pascal's fragments on faith and doubt — the wager, the abyss, and the thinking reed.

planned.title: Ethics
planned.author: Baruch Spinoza
planned.note: Spinoza proves a philosophy like geometry — God, nature, and freedom as one necessary order.

planned.title: Two Treatises of Government
planned.author: John Locke
planned.note: Locke on natural rights and government by consent — the philosophy behind modern liberty.

planned.title: The Principia
planned.author: Isaac Newton
planned.note: Newton's laws of motion and gravity — the mathematical system of the world.

planned.title: Gulliver's Travels
planned.author: Jonathan Swift
planned.note: Swift's voyages to impossible lands — the sharpest satire of human folly ever written.

planned.title: The Spirit of the Laws
planned.author: Montesquieu
planned.note: Montesquieu on what makes laws just — and the separation of powers that shaped every later republic.

planned.title: Candide
planned.author: Voltaire
planned.note: Voltaire's lightning satire — innocence loose in a brutal world, and the case for tending one's garden.

planned.title: The Social Contract
planned.author: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
planned.note: Rousseau on freedom and the general will — 'man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.'

planned.title: The Wealth of Nations
planned.author: Adam Smith
planned.note: The founding work of modern economics — the division of labor and the invisible hand.

planned.title: The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire
planned.author: Edward Gibbon
planned.note: Gibbon's vast, ironic chronicle of how the greatest empire of antiquity came undone.

planned.title: The Critique of Pure Reason
planned.author: Immanuel Kant
planned.note: Kant remakes philosophy — what the mind can know, and the limits it cannot cross.

planned.title: The Federalist Papers
planned.author: Hamilton, Madison & Jay
planned.note: The argument for the American Constitution — the finest writing on how a free republic actually works.

planned.title: Faust
planned.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
planned.note: Goethe's supreme drama — the scholar who wagers his soul for the whole of human experience.

planned.title: Pride and Prejudice
planned.author: Jane Austen
planned.note: Austen's perfect comedy of manners — wit, money, and the slow education of the heart.

planned.title: Democracy in America
planned.author: Alexis de Tocqueville
planned.note: Tocqueville's clear-eyed report on the young United States — democracy's promise and its perils.

planned.title: The Philosophy of History
planned.author: G. W. F. Hegel
planned.note: Hegel reads all of history as the unfolding of freedom — the idea that shaped the modern age.

planned.title: Fear and Trembling
planned.author: Søren Kierkegaard
planned.note: Kierkegaard on Abraham and the leap of faith — the birth of existential thought.

planned.title: Moby-Dick
planned.author: Herman Melville
planned.note: Melville's white whale — an American epic of obsession, the sea, and the unknowable.

planned.title: On Liberty
planned.author: John Stuart Mill
planned.note: Mill's classic argument for individual freedom against the tyranny of the majority.

planned.title: The Origin of Species
planned.author: Charles Darwin
planned.note: The book that remade biology — evolution by natural selection.

planned.title: Great Expectations
planned.author: Charles Dickens
planned.note: Dickens's masterpiece of self-deception — a poor boy, a secret fortune, and the cost of becoming a gentleman.

planned.title: Capital
planned.author: Karl Marx
planned.note: Marx's anatomy of capitalism — labor, value, and the engine he believed would undo it.

planned.title: War and Peace
planned.author: Leo Tolstoy
planned.note: Tolstoy's vast novel of Russia at war with Napoleon — the whole of life held in one book.

planned.title: Middlemarch
planned.author: George Eliot
planned.note: George Eliot's study of a provincial town — the grandest English novel of ordinary lives and thwarted hopes.

planned.title: The Brothers Karamazov
planned.author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
planned.note: Dostoevsky's final novel — a murder, three brothers, and the deepest argument in fiction over God and freedom.

planned.title: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
planned.author: Mark Twain
planned.note: Twain's runaway boy and a freedom-seeking man on a raft — the great American novel of conscience.

planned.title: Beyond Good and Evil
planned.author: Friedrich Nietzsche
planned.note: Nietzsche's assault on inherited morality — and his demand that we create our own values.

planned.title: A Doll's House
planned.author: Henrik Ibsen
planned.note: Ibsen's quiet bombshell — a wife walks out of her marriage, and the modern theater begins.

planned.title: The Principles of Psychology
planned.author: William James
planned.note: William James founds modern psychology — the stream of consciousness, habit, and the self.

planned.title: Heart of Darkness
planned.author: Joseph Conrad
planned.note: Conrad's voyage up the Congo into the heart of empire — and of human darkness.

planned.title: The Interpretation of Dreams
planned.author: Sigmund Freud
planned.note: Freud opens the unconscious — dreams as the royal road to the hidden mind.

planned.title: The Waste Land
planned.author: T. S. Eliot
planned.note: T. S. Eliot's fractured masterpiece — the defining poem of the modern century.

planned.title: Ulysses
planned.author: James Joyce
planned.note: Joyce remakes the novel — one Dublin day rendered whole, the Odyssey turned inside out.

planned.title: The Trial
planned.author: Franz Kafka
planned.note: Kafka's nightmare of a man arrested for a crime never named — the modern condition as parable.
